text:
Maria Nguyen: Heads up — we saw a multi-tenant burst in eu-west that blew out cross-AZ egress and caused 95th p90 latency regression for several small tenants. Not the usual thermal/noisy-GPU signature.
Vishal Rao: seen it. telemetry shows spikes aligned with subnet boundary at 10:02 UTC, sustained ~40s, repeated 3x. egress bytes + connection fanout both high.
Samir Patel: suspects: a training job opening many short-lived connections (data preprocessing) + embeddings runtimes > kvcache churn. Could be tenant-side fanout.
Jess Cho: any dedicated pools impacted? or just shared-slices?
Maria Nguyen: mostly shared slices on racks with the 25Gb uplink. Dedicated pools mostly fine but some fallbacks to shared picked up extra traffic and amplified.
Leo Martin: OpsBot ran the initial alert — OpsBot: detected subnet egress > 80% for /24 eu-west-rack-7 for 120s, flagged candidate noisy tenants: tenant-a, tenant-labs-2.
Maria Nguyen: proposal: "subnet shepherding" — apply transient per-subnet soft cap + progressive fair-backoff signals to allocations talking to that subnet. Purpose: limit blast radius while preserving dedicated SLA.
Vishal Rao: concretely: when subnet egress > threshold -> mark subnet as "shepherded"; scheduler reduces new shared-slice allocations targeting that subnet by 60%, and signals active allocations with a per-alloc token-bucket throttle to drop burst concurrency.
Samir Patel: add to that a passive probe: if tenant shows >90% long-tail connections we inject a small delay (50-200ms) into new connection handshakes via sidecar to discourage fanout. Low risk and reversible.
Jess Cho: how do we avoid harming latency-sensitive Prod tenants that were routed there for locality? We shouldn't throttle dedicated or reserved slices.
Maria Nguyen: reserved/dedicated pools are exempt. We only steer shared allocations and soft-throttle their egress. Also create a short-lived routing rule that prefers sibling-AZ nodes with spare uplink if cross-AZ latency penalty <10ms.
Leo Martin: ops notes: need changes in three places — host-side qdisc shim (tc/htb), scheduler admission controls (allocator), and proxy sidecar throttles. Can we canary in eu-west rack 7?
Vishal Rao: yes. rollout plan: 1) warm qdisc shim in canary host via chef; 2) allocator flag to avoid new shared-slice in shepherded subnets; 3) sidecar feature flag to enable handshake-delay for flagged tenant ids. Canary window 2h then measure 95/99 lat + tail egress.
Samir Patel: metrics to watch: subnet_egress_bytes, conn_count_1m, alloc_fallback_rate, p95_inference_latency, routing_fallbacks. Also track false positives (dedicated marked).
Jess Cho: cost implication? Prefer not to overprovision AZ capacity; fallback steering may increase cross-AZ egress fees temporarily. Need SRE + finance calc for expected delta.
Maria Nguyen: agreed. initial estimate: shifting 15% of shared-slice traffic to sibling AZ could add ~5-8% egress $. But reduces repeated retries and CPU waste — net should be neutral or slightly positive. I'll loop in finance.
OpsBot: action created: #ops-4512345678 Subnet Shepherding canary — assignees @vishal,@maria,@samir.
Leo Martin: who owns the allocator change? @vishal. Host shim: @samir. Sidecar: @jess. We'll sync in 30m in #eng-infra to coordinate.
Vishal Rao: I'll draft the allocator flag PR and include rollback hooks. Plan to gate by metric watch and an automated rollback if p99 latency increases by >10% for protected tenants.
Samir Patel: I'll prototype a minimal tc rule and a small proxy delay patch. Will test on k8s dev cluster first.
Jess Cho: I'll add the sidecar feature flag and a tenant whitelist to avoid hitting prod-critical customers.
Maria Nguyen: thanks — this should keep noisy bursts local and avoid large-scale fallback thrash. Ping after canary and we'll decide whether to bake this into the fairbackoff playbook. :thumbsup:
